headline: Father Busa's Index Thomisticus
text: Father Roberto Busa begins creating a computerized concordance of Thomas Aquinas's writings, often considered the birth of humanities computing.

headline: Computers and the Humanities Journal
text: The first academic journal dedicated to computing in humanities research is established, providing a forum for early digital humanists.

headline: Text Encoding Initiative Founded
text: TEI develops standardized guidelines for encoding humanities texts in XML, becoming fundamental infrastructure for digital text analysis.

headline: The Victorian Web Launches
text: One of the first major hypertext scholarly resources, demonstrating the potential of linked digital scholarship beyond print constraints.

headline: Google Books Project Announced
text: Google begins mass digitization of library collections, making millions of books searchable and readable online, sparking debates about copyright and access.

headline: HathiTrust Research Center Opens
text: Launches providing computational access to millions of digitized volumes for text mining and analysis, enabling large-scale digital humanities research.

headline: Voyant Tools Reaches Maturity
text: This web-based text analysis environment becomes widely adopted for exploratory text mining, making computational methods accessible to humanities scholars.

headline: AI Language Models in DH
text: Large language models like GPT-3 begin being explored for humanities applications including translation, text generation, and historical document analysis.

headline: Multimodal Digital Scholarship
text: Integration of text, image, audio, and video analysis using AI, creating new possibilities for cross-media humanities research.
